title: Share Trading Policy (SG-LSC-GP-2A1, Version 2)
date_approved: 10 November 2020 (document date; approved by the Board)

tiers.name: Team Members
tiers.description: All full-time, part-time and casual employees of the Sigma Group, plus secondees, contractors, consultants and advisers required by their engagement terms or by written notice from the Company Secretary or CEO to comply. Subject to the insider trading prohibition, Closed Periods, the 12-month holding and speculative dealing ban, the short selling and stock lending ban, the unvested-derivatives ban and the margin loan ban. Non-executive Directors are not expressly within this definition.

tiers.name: Specified Persons
tiers.description: List maintained by the Head of Human Resources of persons who possess or are likely to possess inside information: all Directors and officers, KMPs, Executive Leadership Team Members, nominated senior executives, any individual notified in writing by the CEO or Company Secretary, and Associates of all of these. Additionally subject to prior written clearance for every dealing, post-trade confirmation, registry monitoring and system trade blocks.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Any director of the Sigma Group. Specified Persons whose clearance cannot be delegated below the Chairman (the Chairman is cleared by the CEO), who report breaches to the Company Secretary and who notify dealings under their engagement terms for Listing Rule 3.19A and s205G.

tiers.name: Executive Leadership Team Members
tiers.description: Team Members disclosed as ELT members. Specified Persons whose clearance cannot be delegated by the Chairman to the CEO or Company Secretary.

tiers.name: Associates
tiers.description: Spouse or de facto partner, dependants, family members who may influence or be influenced in dealings, and any company, trust or entity controlled (alone or jointly) by the person or those family members. Associates of Specified Persons are themselves Specified Persons; Team Members must take reasonable steps to ensure Associates comply, including not dealing in Closed Periods.

definitions.hedging_definition: a derivative includes any option, forward contract, swap, futures contract or warrant, or any other arrangement, which itself or in combination with one or more other derivatives would have the effect of providing a Sigma Team Member with a greater benefit than would otherwise have been realised in respect of the unvested Sigma Shares

windows.start_anchor: end of Sigma's half-year period (31 July)
windows.end_anchor: close of business on the day after Sigma releases its half year results announcement to the ASX

windows.start_anchor: end of Sigma's full year period (31 January)
windows.end_anchor: close of business on the day after Sigma releases its full year results announcement to the ASX

windows.start_anchor: 21 days immediately preceding the Annual General Meeting

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board of Directors may prohibit dealing at such other times as it determines (section 10); commencement of black-out periods is notified by email alerts. Confidentiality is not addressed.

rules.detail: No derivatives (options, forwards, swaps, futures, warrants or any arrangement giving a greater benefit than the unvested shares would realise) over unvested Sigma Shares; no clearance route.
rules.evidence: Sigma Team Members are not permitted to use derivatives in relation to any unvested Sigma Shares.

rules.detail: Derivatives over vested shares are allowed only if the shares are not subject to a holding lock.
rules.evidence: Sigma Team Members may use derivatives in relation to Sigma Shares which have vested, provided any dealing in those derivatives complies with the other requirements of this policy and the Sigma Shares are not subject to a holding lock.

rules.detail: Derivatives over vested, unlocked shares are expressly permitted if the dealing complies with the rest of the policy. The Derivatives definition names put and call options, forwards, CFDs, caps and collars and OTC instruments deriving value from Sigma Shares, and Sigma Shares includes securities deriving value from Sigma securities, so a collar is a dealing in Sigma Shares requiring prior written clearance from the Chairman, outside Closed Periods, and subject to the 12-month and speculative dealing rules.
rules.evidence: put or call options, exchange traded options, forward contracts, futures, warrants, depositary receipts, structured financial products, swaps, contracts for difference, spread bets, caps and collars and any other hedging or investment arrangement that derives value from the relevant underlying security or asset.

rules.detail: Team Members who are not Specified Persons may use derivatives over vested, unlocked shares without clearance, subject to Closed Periods, the 12-month holding rule and the insider trading prohibition.
rules.evidence: Sigma Team Members may use derivatives in relation to Sigma Shares which have vested, provided any dealing in those derivatives complies with the other requirements of this policy and the Sigma Shares are not subject to a holding lock.

rules.detail: The unvested-derivatives ban is expressly an anti-hedging rule: arrangements that let a Team Member realise value from unvested shares regardless of performance hurdles are barred.
rules.evidence: The use of derivatives over unvested Sigma Shares has the potential to allow Sigma Team Members to realise value from those securities even if the performance hurdles have not been satisfied.

rules.detail: Hedging arrangements are Derivatives and cannot be used over shares under a holding lock.
rules.evidence: the Sigma Shares are not subject to a holding lock.

rules.detail: Hedging is not separately defined; 'any other hedging or investment arrangement' is a Derivative, permitted over vested unlocked shares with prior written clearance from the Chairman. The policy encourages long-term shareholding but imposes no general hedging ban for directors or executives.
rules.evidence: caps and collars and any other hedging or investment arrangement that derives value from the relevant underlying security or asset.

rules.detail: Non-Specified Team Members may hedge vested, unlocked shares without clearance subject to the other policy rules.
rules.evidence: Sigma Team Members may use derivatives in relation to Sigma Shares which have vested

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward is a forward contract (a Derivative) and an agreement to dispose (a dealing), permitted over vested unlocked shares with clearance, but any arrangement that could result in disposal within 12 months of acquisition is banned and a structure secured on the shares is caught by the margin loan ban.
rules.evidence: 'Deal' or 'dealing' means applying for, acquiring or disposing of securities, or entering an agreement to do any of those things.

rules.detail: Outright ban on short selling arrangements in relation to Sigma Shares.
rules.evidence: Similarly, Sigma Team Members are prohibited from entering short selling or stock lending arrangements in relation to Sigma Shares.

rules.detail: Outright ban on stock lending arrangements in relation to Sigma Shares, so a collar cannot be supported by lending the collared shares to the bank.
rules.evidence: Similarly, Sigma Team Members are prohibited from entering short selling or stock lending arrangements in relation to Sigma Shares.

rules.detail: CFDs and spread bets are named Derivatives and so dealings in Sigma Shares. They are banned over unvested shares and, as leveraged short-term instruments, fall within the ban on dealing as a short-term trader or on a speculative basis; a short CFD is also short selling in substance.
rules.evidence: Sigma Team Members must not deal in Sigma Shares as a short-term trader or on a speculative basis.

rules.detail: Margin loans to fund acquisition of Sigma Shares, or in relation to which Sigma Shares may be used as security, are prohibited because their terms may compel a sale in a Closed Period or while holding inside information. Margin loans are also cited as arrangements that could result in disposal within 12 months.
rules.evidence: Team Members are prohibited from entering margin loan arrangements to fund the acquisition of Sigma Shares or in relation to which Sigma Shares may be used as security against loan repayment.

rules.detail: Granting a charge, mortgage or pledge is not named and the dealing definition does not list it, though 'granting ... any beneficial interest in securities' is a dealing example. The only express restriction is the margin loan ban.

Only 'margin loan arrangements' are named, but the ban extends to any such arrangement 'in relation to which Sigma Shares may be used as security against loan repayment' and the stated rationale (lender-compelled sale in a Closed Period) applies to any loan secured on Sigma Shares. Section 11 separately bars arrangements that could result in disposal within 12 months of acquisition. A non-margin secured loan over shares held more than 12 months is not expressly addressed.
rules.evidence: Margin loans to support an investment in Sigma Shares can compromise compliance with this policy, as the terms of the loan may compel the sale of Sigma Shares during a Closed Period or when the Team Member has relevant inside information.

rules.detail: 12-month minimum holding from acquisition, extending to arrangements (margin loans given as the example) that could result in disposal within 12 months, plus a ban on short-term or speculative dealing. Carve-outs for shares from options held 12 months, LTI/SPP/Employee Share Plan shares and pro-rata rights.
rules.evidence: Sigma Team Members who acquire Sigma Shares must not dispose of those shares, or enter arrangements (such as margin loans) which could result in those shares being disposed of, within 12 months of acquisition.

clearance.approver: Chairman (or CEO where the Chairman is unavailable), obtained via the Company Secretary on the Schedule 1 form; the Chairman must first inform and obtain written clearance from the CEO for the Chairman's own dealings. Not delegable.
clearance.post_trade_to: Company (per Director engagement terms for Listing Rule 3.19A and s205G)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: per engagement terms (Listing Rule 3.19A: 5 business days)
clearance.evidence: In the case of clearance required in respect of the Chairman, the Chairman must first inform and obtain written clearance from the CEO.

clearance.approver: Chairman (or CEO where the Chairman is unavailable), via the Company Secretary on the Schedule 1 form. Not delegable.
clearance.post_trade_to: Company Secretary (CEO for the Company Secretary): written confirmation of details of any dealing by the Specified Person or their Associates
clearance.post_trade_deadline: within three business days after the dealing is completed
clearance.evidence: A clearance to undertake the proposed dealing will be valid for two business days (but completion of the proposed dealing must not occur during a blackout period and must otherwise comply with the requirements of this policy).

clearance.approver: Chairman (or CEO where unavailable) via the Company Secretary; for Specified Persons who are not Directors or ELT Members the Chairman may delegate the decision to the CEO or Company Secretary (Chairman or CEO decide for the Company Secretary's own trades). Registry system clearance applies to Employee Incentive Plan trades and off-market issuer-sponsored transfers are blocked without clearance.
clearance.post_trade_to: Company Secretary (CEO for the Company Secretary)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: within three business days after the dealing is completed
clearance.evidence: The Chairman may choose to delegate the decision to grant a clearance to trade to a Specified Person who is not a Director or an Executive Leadership Team Member to the CEO or the Company Secretary
If your role makes you a Specified Person then additional restrictions apply to you and your Associates: Only deal in shares issued by Sigma when cleared to do so

short_term.basis: from acquisition; extends to arrangements (such as margin loans) that could result in disposal within 12 months
carve_outs: shares acquired through the exercise of an option or similar right where the option or right has been held for at least 12 months
shares acquired under Sigma's Long Term Incentive Plan, Share Purchase Plan or Employee Share Plan
share rights acquired pursuant to a pro-rata entitlement offer to all Sigma shareholders
short_term.evidence: Sigma Team Members who acquire Sigma Shares must not dispose of those shares, or enter arrangements (such as margin loans) which could result in those shares being disposed of, within 12 months of acquisition.

exceptions.approver: Chairman (CEO for the Chairman), who may obtain legal advice at Sigma's expense and require evidence
exceptions.evidence: A pressing financial commitment on the part of the Specified Person, Team Member or relevant contractor that cannot otherwise be satisfied; Severe financial hardship

Where there is a court order, or there are court enforceable undertakings to transfer or sell Sigma Shares (for example a bona-fide family settlement) or there is some other overriding legal or regulatory requirement to do so.

Accepting, or undertaking to accept, an offer for Sigma Shares made under a takeover bid. ... Disposing of Sigma Shares under a court approved compromise or arrangement under Part 5.1 of the Corporations Act, or under an equal access scheme buy-back or equal reduction of capital

Disposing of rights acquired, or acquiring Sigma Shares, under a rights issue offered to all or most of the ordinary shareholders of Sigma ... acquiring Sigma Shares under, any dividend reinvestment plan or security purchase plan made available to all or most of the ordinary shareholders of Sigma.

applications to participate in the relevant Plan; acquisitions of shares (as applicable) under the relevant Plan; and variations of instructions in relation to levels of participation in the relevant Plan, may be made at any time whether during the Closed Period(s) or not.
Accepting an offer of, or invitation to apply for, Sigma Shares made in (or accompanied by) a prospectus or product disclosure statement.

Consequential dealing in any Sigma Shares that occurs as a result of the Specified Person or their Associate holding, acquiring or dealing in units, shares or other securities of a managed investment scheme, listed investment company, exchange-traded fund or similar investment vehicle that is managed by a third party

Where the Specified Person or their Associate is a trustee, dealing in Sigma Shares by the trust provided that neither the Specified Person nor any Associate is a beneficiary of the trust and any decision to trade is taken by another trustee or by an investment manager independently

An off-market transaction involving the transfer or other disposal of any Sigma Shares from a Specified Person (or their Associate) to, or to a Specified Person (or their Associate) from, any of the following: an Associate of the Specified Person ...; a company, trust or other entity over which the relevant Specified Person or an Associate of the Specified Person has control or significant influence ...; or a superannuation fund

An off-market transaction in any Sigma Shares where no or only nominal consideration is given or received by the Specified Person or any of their Associates in respect of the relevant transaction (including a transfer of Sigma Shares by the legal personal representative of any person to a beneficiary of that person's estate).

external_documents: Director engagement terms (notification obligations for Listing Rule 3.19A and s205G)
exemption_authority: Chairman (CEO for the Chairman) may grant special dispensation to trade in a prohibited period for extraordinary circumstances, exercised sparingly, with legal advice available at Sigma's expense and evidence required; the Chairman also approves clearance timeframes beyond two business days. Board approves the Policy and can prohibit dealing at other times.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Derivatives ... includes the following if they relate to or derive value from Sigma Shares ...: put or call options, exchange traded options, forward contracts, futures, warrants, depositary receipts, structured financial products, swaps, contracts for difference, spread bets, caps and collars and any other hedging or investment arrangement
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An OTC collar is squarely a Derivative and, through the Sigma Shares definition, a dealing in Sigma Shares requiring Chairman clearance and subject to Closed Periods and the unvested/holding-lock ban.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Sigma Team Members may use derivatives in relation to Sigma Shares which have vested, provided any dealing in those derivatives complies with the other requirements of this policy and the Sigma Shares are not subject to a holding lock.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no general hedging ban for directors or executives; the put and call legs over vested, unlocked shares are expressly contemplated.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Team Members are prohibited from entering margin loan arrangements to fund the acquisition of Sigma Shares or in relation to which Sigma Shares may be used as security against loan repayment.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg secured on the collared shares is caught if characterised as a margin loan arrangement; the stated rationale (lender-compelled sale in a Closed Period) means a bank facility with LVR triggers or enforcement rights is likely treated the same way.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Sigma Team Members who acquire Sigma Shares must not dispose of those shares, or enter arrangements (such as margin loans) which could result in those shares being disposed of, within 12 months of acquisition.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar with physical settlement or a secured loan with enforcement rights over shares acquired within the past 12 months is a prohibited arrangement; the collar should cover only shares held (or LTI/SPP/ESP shares acquired) at least 12 months earlier or fall within the carve-outs.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Sigma Team Members are prohibited from entering short selling or stock lending arrangements in relation to Sigma Shares.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank cannot borrow the collared shares from the executive to hedge its own position or to structure the facility as a securities loan.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Team Member means any full time, part time or casual employee of any member of Sigma Group and extends to any secondee, contractor or consultant of, or adviser to, any member of Sigma Group whose terms of engagement require them, or who have been given written notice ... to comply with this policy as though they were an employee.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Sections 11 and 12 (12-month holding, derivatives, margin loans) are addressed to Team Members, so their application to non-executive Directors, who are Specified Persons but not employees, depends on their engagement terms.

bespoke_clauses.clause: No clearance to trade will be given during a Closed Period as these are periods when the risk of insider trading, or the appearance of insider trading is high.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Entry, roll, unwind and settlement of the collar must all fall in open periods; only the Chairman's extraordinary-circumstances dispensation can override this.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A clearance to undertake the proposed dealing will be valid for two business days ... Timeframes beyond 2 days require the approval of the Sigma Chairman.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar must be priced and executed within two business days of clearance unless the Chairman approves a longer window.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A clearance to trade should not be granted where: there is a matter in relation to which inside information in respect of Sigma Shares (whether the Specified Person knows about the matter or not) when the Specified Person requests clearance or proposes to deal in Sigma Shares
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Clearance can be refused without reasons because of a matter the executive is unaware of, and refusal must be kept confidential from the bank.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the blocking of off market dealings for Specified Persons where shares are held through issuer sponsored holdings without prior clearance ... monitor all trades by Specified Person via share registry trading alerts
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Transfer of issuer-sponsored shares to a bank custodian or nominee will be blocked at the registry without clearance and any movement will be flagged to the Company Secretary.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The additional restrictions on Specified Persons in Chapter 4 do not apply to dealing by a Specified Person or their Associate that constitutes or involves, or results directly from, any of the acts or circumstances set out below.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The section 17 exceptions relieve only the clearance requirement, not the Closed Period, 12-month or margin loan rules, and there is no secured-lender enforcement exception.

bespoke_clauses.clause: a company, trust or other entity that A or any of their family members referred to above controls (whether alone or jointly with each other)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar or loan entered through a family trust or controlled company is treated as the Specified Person's own dealing and needs clearance.

summary: The collar legs are available but the loan leg is doubtful. Derivatives, with collars and OTC put and call options expressly named, may be used over vested Sigma Shares that are not under a holding lock, so a director or executive who is a Specified Person can enter the put and call with prior written clearance from the Chairman (CEO for the Chairman), valid for two business days, outside the 31 July, 31 January and pre-AGM Closed Periods, with post-trade confirmation within three business days. Derivatives over unvested shares are absolutely prohibited, stock lending and short selling are banned, and no arrangement that could result in disposal within 12 months of acquiring the shares is permitted, so the collar should cover shares held for at least 12 months (or LTI/SPP/ESP shares). The loan secured on the collared shares is caught by section 12 if it is a 'margin loan arrangement in relation to which Sigma Shares may be used as security'; the policy's stated concern is lender-compelled sales in Closed Periods, so a facility with LVR triggers or enforcement rights is likely prohibited, while a non-margin secured loan over shares held more than 12 months is not expressly addressed and would need the Chairman's clearance. Sections 11 and 12 are addressed to Team Members, leaving their application to non-executive Directors to their engagement terms.
